name: Ride a horse at walk and trot
blurb: Riding is a partnership with a large animal that has its own opinions. Lessons are non-negotiable — this is not one to teach yourself.
gear: Lessons at a reputable riding school
A properly fitted riding hat to current safety standard
Boots with a small heel, and gloves
steps: Learn ground safety first: how to approach, lead and stand beside a horse without getting stood on or startled.
Learn to mount and dismount correctly, and to check the girth and stirrup length.
Learn the basic position: heels down, shoulders back, a straight line from ear to shoulder to hip to heel.
Learn to sit the walk and to steer with your seat and legs, not by pulling on the reins.
Learn rising trot, matching the rhythm and the correct diagonal.
Learn to stop and slow with your body first, and to fall safely.
tips: Balancing on the reins hurts the horse’s mouth and unbalances you. Balance comes from the seat.
Always wear a current-standard hat. Head injuries are the main serious risk in riding.
proof: You can tack up with supervision, walk, trot and steer independently in a school lesson.
